rawCommits.subject: feat(onboarding): add two-lane first-run flow (#88)
rawCommits.body:
* feat(onboarding): two-lane onboarding — Just Start or Set Up My Agent

Replace the auto-opening 6-step wizard with a two-lane choice screen:

Lane 1 — Just Start:
- Relies on the existing ensureCeoHome() auto-provisioning
- Desktop: navigates to /chat with a one-shot folder prompt banner
- Web: navigates straight to /chat
- Zero configuration, user customizes later in settings

Lane 2 — Set Up My Agent:
- Opens the existing wizard, shortened from 6 steps to 3
- Keeps: Identity (avatar + personality), Expertise (skills), Launch
- Removes: Integrations, Connections, Automations (data was never
  applied during onboarding — code comments say 'deferred, post-signup')
- Step components are kept on disk for future reuse

New components:
- OnboardingChoice: two-card GlassModal with surface-aware text
- ProjectFolderPrompt: desktop-only dismissable banner in chat
- folder-prompt-storage: localStorage one-shot flag

Also:
- agent-store gains firstRunDetected flag (set before ensureCeoHome)
- Analytics event: onboarding_lane_selected with lane value
- Mobile layout: cards stack vertically at <=680px

* fix(onboarding): address review findings — unlatch firstRun, scope storage per-user, add in-memory fallback

1. firstRunDetected false-positive: unlatch the flag when a subsequent
   org-scoped fetch finds agents (the prior unscoped fetch with null
   activeOrgId could falsely trigger it).

2. Folder prompt key now per-user: setFolderPromptUser(userId) scopes
   the localStorage key so multi-account desktops don't bleed state.

3. OnboardingChoice in-memory fallback: if localStorage is blocked
   (private mode / quota), the in-memory Set still suppresses the
   modal for the current session so it can't become undismissable.

4. Bundle budget: confirmed already failing on main (1,188,465 main
   vs 1,188,225 branch — branch is 240 bytes smaller). Not a
   regression from this PR.

* fix(onboarding): address round-2 review findings

1. Revert the firstRunDetected unlatch — the previous fix (clearing
   the flag when a subsequent fetch finds agents) would race with
   ensureCeoHome: the auto-created CEO makes the next fetch return
   agents, clearing the flag before the user picks a lane. The flag
   now latches once and is only cleared on logout. OnboardingChoice
   suppresses itself via its own localStorage/in-memory choice flag,
   which is the correct layer for this decision.

2. Wire up setFolderPromptUser — OnboardingChoice now calls
   setFolderPromptUser(userId) before markFolderPromptPending(), and
   ProjectFolderPrompt calls it before isFolderPromptPending(). The
   storage key is now actually per-user on multi-account desktops.

3. Lazy-load OnboardingChoice — moved from static import to
   lazy(() => import(...)) with Suspense fallback={null} so
   agent-store and its dependencies are not in the public/logged-out
   startup graph.

* fix(onboarding): require org-scoped fetch for firstRun, gate lazy chunk behind auth

1. firstRunDetected false-positive: only latch the flag when
   activeOrgId is set (org state has settled). The early unscoped
   fetch (activeOrgId === undefined) can return empty for existing
   users whose agents are only visible under their org — that empty
   list is not authoritative. A true new user will still trigger
   the flag on the org-scoped fetch that follows.

2. Gate OnboardingChoice render behind isAuthenticated so the lazy
   chunk is never requested for public/logged-out visitors. The
   lazy() import keeps it out of the static graph, and the auth
   gate prevents React from even mounting the Suspense boundary
   until the user is signed in.

* fix(onboarding): defer ensureCeoHome until org-scoped fetch to preserve first-run signal

The previous fix gated firstRunDetected behind activeOrgId, but still
ran ensureCeoHome() during the unscoped empty fetch. This created the
CEO before the org-scoped refetch arrived, so the refetch found agents
and never set firstRunDetected — hiding the choice modal from real new
users.

Now the entire empty-list branch (firstRunDetected + ensureCeoHome +
commitAgents) only runs when activeOrgId is set. The unscoped pre-org
fetch commits an empty agent list and exits, leaving CEO creation to
the authoritative org-scoped fetch that follows.

Flow for a new user:
  1. Unscoped fetch → empty → commit empty, no CEO created
  2. Org settles → org-scoped fetch → empty → latch firstRunDetected,
     run ensureCeoHome, create CEO, commit
  3. OnboardingChoice sees firstRunDetected → shows modal

Flow for an existing user:
  1. Unscoped fetch → empty → commit empty, no CEO created
  2. Org settles → org-scoped fetch → finds agents → agents.length > 0
     branch, no firstRunDetected

* fix(onboarding): make firstRunDetected a latched, authority-gated decision

The first-run signal kept regressing because "empty agent list" was being
read at moments when the list's scope wasn't trustworthy. This commit makes
the state machine explicit:

1. Authority requires a network-confirmed org roster. org-store gains
   `orgsResolved`, set only by a successful network refreshOrgs() (the
   IndexedDB org cache can be stale) and cleared on logout/refresh start.
   An empty list may decide the first-run question only when the roster is
   resolved AND the fetch was scoped to the settled org — or the roster
   proved the user has zero orgs, in which case the unscoped own-agents
   list IS the full picture (previously a zero-org new user never got a
   CEO or the onboarding choice at all).

2. The decision latches once per signed-in session
   (firstRunSignalSettledThisSession). Any fetch returning agents closes
   the question as "not first run"; the first authoritative empty closes
   it as "first run" — recorded BEFORE ensureCeoHome creates the default
   CEO. Later empty results (switching to a freshly created empty org)
   can no longer flip firstRunDetected on for existing users.

3. The swallowed-refetch race is fixed. When the org settles while the
   initial unscoped fetch is in flight, the org subscription's forced
   refetch was returned the in-flight promise and dropped — the org only
   settles once, so nothing retried and a new user saw no CEO/onboarding
   until the 30s TTL. fetchAgents now re-runs itself from finally() when
   the org scope drifted (org id changed, or authority rose while the
   committed list is still empty).

4. The org subscription fires on authority rising, not just org-id
   change, covering the cached-org-confirmed and zero-org cases where the
   id never changes at settle time (skipped when a fleet is already
   painted, so the common warm path stays at one fetch).

5. Auth identity changes (including direct A->B account switches that
   never pass through signed-out) now fully reset the store and both
   per-session latches, so one user's firstRunDetected/agents can't leak
   into the next session.

Adds state-machine tests driving auth/org settle timing for all four
onboarding scenarios plus the mid-flight settle race, zero-org users,
mid-session org switches, and account switches.

rendered.title: First-run onboarding gets a two-lane choice, plus chat routing that actually remembers where you were
rendered.intro: Today's nightly reworks the very first moments in Aura and tightens the chat surface around it. New users now pick between "Just Start" and "Set Up My Agent" instead of being dropped into a six-step wizard, and the chat app learned to preserve, restore, and share concrete session routes across taskbar returns, fresh canvases, and public visitors. The desktop shell also stops flashing hidden windows in CI, and the public chat's free-message limit finally has a real UI.

entries.title: Fresh chat canvases bind to a real session after first send
entries.summary: The chat app's fresh-canvas flow now correctly hands off to the persisted session route as soon as the first message materializes, without racing the session list.

items.text: Fresh chat routes now consistently flag as pending until a session exists, and the fresh canvas key is threaded through to the standalone chat hook so the next send is armed as a new session exactly once per canvas.

After a fresh send lands, ChatAppRoute swaps the `fresh=` param for a full `session/project/instance/agent` URL via a replace navigation, so reloads and back-navigation land on the real session instead of a blank canvas.
Share links from the message actions menu now read the canonical `project`/`instance`/`session` params from the URL, fixing shares started from agent-scoped stream keys.

entries.title: macOS desktop launches visibly, CI stays headless
entries.summary: The desktop shell now opens its main window on launch for real users while suppressing it on CI runners so automated builds don't pop UI.

items.text: The macOS main window is shown on launch by default, restoring the expected first-open behavior for desktop users.
Standard CI environments are detected via env and keep the desktop window hidden, so builds and headless tests no longer flash a window.

entries.title: Taskbar returns, session hydration, and mobile public chat polish
entries.summary: The chat app now remembers the concrete session route you last had open, the web session list survives malformed data and legacy API hosts, and the mobile public chat shell gets a touch-friendly refresh.

items.text: Opening chat from the taskbar or nav rail restores the exact `session/project/instance/agent` route you were last on, including derivation from legacy session-only links, while fresh canvases are explicitly not remembered.

Web session hydration is hardened: SessionsList tolerates a polluted `sessions` prop by rendering the empty state, and host-config canonicalizes the legacy Render API origin to `https://api.aura.ai` on production web even when a stale value is stored.
The mobile public chat shell bumps top-bar and button targets to 48px with safe-area-aware padding, adds `touch-action: manipulation`, and ships new copy for the free-message limit state.

entries.title: Public chat gets a real free-limit gate
entries.summary: When a public visitor hits the free-message cap, the composer is replaced with a titled notice and login/sign-up actions instead of surfacing a raw error.

items.text: PublicChatView detects the limit-reached error, swaps the input bar for a rounded limit notice with title, body, and primary/secondary CTAs, and mirrors the same handling in the mobile view so streams stop cleanly at the cap.
New localized strings introduce a dedicated title, body, and placeholder for the free-chat limit state driving both the desktop and mobile public views.

entries.title: Two-lane first-run onboarding replaces the six-step wizard
entries.summary: New users now see a two-card choice — Just Start or Set Up My Agent — backed by a latched, authority-gated first-run signal so the modal only appears for genuine new accounts.

items.text: The auto-opening 6-step wizard is replaced by an OnboardingChoice modal: Just Start relies on `ensureCeoHome()` auto-provisioning and (on desktop) shows a one-shot project folder prompt banner, while Set Up My Agent opens the wizard trimmed to Identity, Expertise, and Launch. Lane selection is instrumented via an `onboarding_lane_selected` analytics event.

`firstRunDetected` is now a latched, authority-gated decision in agent-store: it only settles once per signed-in session and only from an org-scoped fetch (or a confirmed zero-org roster), so existing users switching into an empty org can no longer be misclassified as new.

`ensureCeoHome` is deferred until the org-scoped fetch, and a swallowed-refetch race is fixed by re-running `fetchAgents` when the org scope drifts — so a brand-new user reliably gets a default CEO and sees the onboarding choice instead of waiting for a 30s TTL.

OnboardingChoice is lazy-loaded and gated behind `isAuthenticated`, the folder-prompt storage key is scoped per user with an in-memory fallback when localStorage is blocked, and account switches fully reset the store so one user's onboarding state can't leak into another's session.

highlights: New two-lane first-run onboarding replaces the 6-step wizard
Fresh chat canvases now adopt a real session URL after the first send
Taskbar returns preserve the exact chat session route
Public chat has a proper free-limit gate with login CTAs
macOS desktop window shows on launch but stays hidden in CI
